answer_1.quote: Our alignment method takes a corpus of social media posts (e.g., tweets) from an online community and creates a set of demonstrations (instruction-response pairs) based on the posts. In each demonstration, as shown in Figure , the instruction specifies the task (e.g., tweet generation) with the response being the exact tweet.
datasets: 2.6M tweets from 557K users from October 2022 to March 2023 using ED-related keywords
answer_1.outputs: synthetic corpus D f t i by prompting an LLM f ′ i aligned to the community to generate tweets

answer_2.quote: We compute the semantic embeddings of D i , D f t i , and D context i using BERTweet . We then measure the distance between these embeddings using the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID).

answer_4.quote: An annotator with expertise in EDs on social media was presented with 300 triplets, 50 from each community, where a triplet consists of a community name, a LLM-Context-generated tweet and a finetuned LLM-generated tweet.
answer_4.guideline: For each triplet, the annotator was asked to decide which tweet was more aligned with the given community, by referring to the following characteristics: mis/use of ingroup language, references to themes in underlying distribution (e.g. the Body Image community often references nudity), use of capitalization, and coherence of message.
criteria: references to themes in underlying distribution
